summary: The maintained release publisher source distinguishes a prior attempted-but-unknown tag request from evidence that no historical write occurred. The source-prepared original-intent profile authenticates pinned native operation/result bytes and exact retained journal state, then requires fresh physical/source/admission gates. Independently matching lightweight tag bytes permit only one settlement; authenticated absence permits no send without a separately approved credential factory and uncertainty admission. A selected create-only send has one durable local attempt entry, no redirect or automatic retry, no same-invocation settlement, and no next effect even after HTTP201. A local exclusive entry bounds this invocation; it proves neither historical non-dispatch nor global exactly-once execution. The production factory is deliberately unavailable: source preparation and inert tests do not establish credentials, current effect authority, installation or release completion. Changed provider dependency pins require explicit reviewed compatibility closure; ancestry alone cannot approve the change. Safe bounded write diagnostics retain allowlisted request evidence while instrumentation failures preserve the original provider outcome; they cannot reconstruct a missing original response. Actions result archives use the maintained bounded artifact-reader request semantics, not release-asset octet-stream negotiation. The real recovery path must authenticate the pinned original archive through its actual Request/read loop in inert controls; replacing that reader with archive bytes cannot qualify HTTP transport. Unsupported media refusal propagates once with no fallback, journal mutation or provider send. The source header correction preserves archive/digest/member bindings, deadlines, redirect limits and authorization stripping; it does not establish native preflight acceptance or reconstruct the earlier unknown tag response.
title: Bound original tag-intent uncertainty to one selected operation
